messages.content: I need a first pass on a Raleigh-Durham trip. It is a Cary specialty hospital, training Wednesday and Thursday, and they may want me there Tuesday evening for a dry run. Can you help me sketch flights, hotel location, and whether this is a rental-car trip?

Yes. A few details will make the first pass useful: what week is it, what time are the Wednesday and Thursday sessions, and are you carrying any training equipment or just laptop clothes? For flights, I can compare a late nonstop against an earlier one-stop if the Tuesday dry run becomes real.

Week of May 14. Sessions are roughly 8:30 to 4 both days. Tuesday dry run would be around 5 p.m., not confirmed yet. For now assume carry-on and laptop, but a training case could get added. Hotel should be well reviewed and keep the Cary commute easy. Pool or fitness would be nice; hot tub is a bonus, not the whole trip.

I would structure it as two tracks. Dry-run protected: leave Denver Tuesday morning or early midday with one connection and land RDU around early afternoon, giving time for bag claim, hotel stop, and a 5 p.m. Cary arrival. Downside: less pleasant departure and connection risk. No dry run: take the late-afternoon Denver to RDU nonstop, arriving around 9:30 p.m.; cleanest flight, but it gives up Tuesday setup. For hotels, the Cary office-park cluster is the practical fit: roughly 10 to 15 minutes to the hospital, several solid 4-plus reviewed options, usually pool and fitness, hot tub listings inconsistent. RDU/RTP hotels have better amenity odds but add 25 to 35 minutes each training morning. Rideshare works if it is just you and bags; rent if the case appears.
Do not bother with downtown Raleigh. If Tuesday is not firm, which track would you personally pick? Return Thursday after 6 if possible.

If Tuesday stays optional, I would pick the late nonstop outbound, a Cary hotel, and rideshares. It avoids a connection and gets you in the night before the real sessions. For Thursday, look for a nonstop or clean one-stop after 6:30 p.m.; with a 4 p.m. finish, leaving Cary around 4:45 should usually be enough for RDU if you are not checking bulky gear.
How much should I care about the Cary hotel missing a hot tub? I just need to reset after standing all day.

For this trip, I would not let the hot tub pull you to the airport. A nearby hotel with good reviews, pool, and fitness room will probably help more than a better amenity set that costs you an hour of driving across two mornings.
Okay. Give me a ranked first plan I can send my manager, with the risk note.

Ranked plan: 1. Safe if dry run happens: one-stop outbound landing early afternoon, Cary hotel, rental car if equipment is involved. Best operationally; trade-off is an earlier departure and a connection. 2. Lean if only Wednesday and Thursday: late-afternoon nonstop to RDU, Cary hotel, rideshares. Lowest friction; risk is no Tuesday setup buffer. 3. Amenity-heavy fallback: RDU/RTP suite hotel with pool, hot tub, and fitness plus a rental car. Better recovery amenities, worse commute and more morning variability on I-40. Budget note: Cary hotels look like the sensible spend unless the airport property is dramatically cheaper.
If I rent, should I plan on returning the car Thursday evening? And will a regular car handle the checked training case if they add it?

Yes, return it at RDU before the Thursday flight. If the case is added, book at least a midsize car or compact SUV so you are not wrestling with trunk space. Also budget time for gas and rental return; the case makes rideshares less attractive, especially with a suburban hotel and hospital.
Let us not book until they confirm Tuesday. What exactly should I ask the client by Friday?

Ask them to confirm by Friday noon whether the Tuesday 5 p.m. dry run is required. Also ask whether you must bring the training case, whether shipping to the hospital is possible, where to park or unload, and the exact Cary address for the setup room. Decision rule: if Tuesday is firm, book the early one-stop, Cary hotel, and rental car; if not, book the late nonstop, Cary hotel, and rideshares unless the case gets added.

messages.content: Raleigh update: the Cary client made the Tuesday dry run firm for 5 p.m., and now I do need to bring one checked training case. I need to choose the flight, hotel, and car so I can book today.

Then I would drop the late-afternoon nonstop for the outbound. It lands too late to be useful for setup. Best fit is the earlier one-stop that lands RDU in the early afternoon with a connection around an hour or a little more. The later one-stop that lands closer to 4 p.m. is too tight with a checked case. For hotel, the closer Cary option still looks stronger than the airport suite hotel. And with the case, this becomes a rental-car trip.
Yes, return Thursday after the session. I do not love an extremely early departure, but the dry run matters more.

Use the earliest reasonable option, not the last possible one. I would take the one-stop through Dulles that leaves Denver in the 7 a.m. hour, has roughly a 70 to 80 minute connection, and reaches RDU shortly after 2 p.m. That leaves enough time for bag claim, rental pickup, hotel check-in or bag drop, and getting to Cary. The midmorning connection arriving around 4 p.m. is not enough buffer.
Hotel still worries me a little. The Cary one has pool and fitness but no listed hot tub. Airport suite has all three.

For this schedule, choose the Cary hotel. It is well reviewed, closer to the hospital, has pool and fitness, and avoids a long commute before both classroom days. The airport suite hotel is better on amenities, but the extra driving cuts into the same recovery time the hot tub is supposed to help with.
Fair. Compact SUV or regular sedan?

Compact SUV if the price difference is modest. It gives you easier loading for the training case and keeps the cabin from getting crowded. Pick it up at RDU Tuesday after landing and return it Thursday before the flight. Do not leave the case visible in the vehicle overnight.
What return should I use Thursday? Session ends around 3:30 or 4, then I need to repack.

Book the 7:20-ish nonstop back to Denver if it is still available. That gives you a workable sequence: finish by 4, repack and leave Cary around 5, fuel up, return the car, and get through bag check. I would avoid anything before 6:30 p.m. and avoid adding a connection on the way home unless the nonstop disappears.
Okay, book the early one-stop outbound, the Thursday evening nonstop home, the Cary hotel Tuesday and Wednesday nights, and the compact SUV. Main cabin, and grab a window seat if one is open.

That is the right booking package. Book main cabin so seat selection and changes are easier, add the checked training case to the outbound and return, and select a window where available. Hotel: Cary Tuesday and Wednesday nights, note pool and fitness but no listed hot tub, and request a quiet room away from elevators. Car: compact SUV from RDU Tuesday early afternoon to Thursday early evening. Before you finalize, confirm the hospital loading area, parking instructions, and whether they have a secure place for the case during lunch or overnight.

messages.content: Quick Raleigh check. The airline shortened my outbound connection and now it is only about 38 minutes. The seat map also stopped clearly showing the window I picked. Since I am checking the training case, should I move to the earlier departure?

Yes, if the earlier departure keeps the same single-connection structure and restores a safer layover. A 38-minute connection with a checked training case is too thin before a 5 p.m. dry run. I would not reopen the whole plan, but I would fix that outbound.
Earlier one leaves Denver at 6:40 instead of 7:25, gives me a 1 hour 18 minute connection, and lands RDU at 1:35. Fare difference is $42.

Take it. The $42 buys real protection: more transfer time for you, better odds the checked case makes the connection, and more margin for rental pickup before Cary. Keep the Thursday evening return as booked.
Do I need to call the hotel about late arrival even though this should get me in early afternoon?

Yes, add a late-arrival note anyway. It protects you if the connection slips and costs nothing. Also confirm parking, whether they can hold a room if you arrive after dinner, and whether checkout Thursday can be noon.
For seats, second leg has 18F open. First leg only says assigned, no actual map.

Select 18F on the second leg now. For the first leg, call or use chat to verify the assigned seat; if no window is available, take a forward aisle rather than a bad middle, then check again at the 24-hour mark.
Okay. Give me the final checklist and I will stop poking at it.

Final checklist: switch outbound to the 6:40 departure with the 1 hour 18 minute connection; keep the Thursday evening nonstop. Reconfirm seats, especially the unclear first leg, and select 18F on the second. Add or verify the checked training case both ways, including weight and tag to RDU. Call the Cary hotel for late-arrival note, parking, and noon checkout. Keep compact SUV pickup tied to the new arrival time. Check Denver and RDU weather the night before, save the hospital loading instructions, and leave extra time at DEN because the case is operationally important.
